text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a practice where developers regularly add their code to a shared project. Every time someone makes a change, automated builds start immediately. These builds check that the new code works correctly with the rest of the project. During the build, the system also runs tests to make sure nothing has broken. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become big problems. CI pipelines organise all these steps, from building to testing, so the process happens automatically and quickly. As a result, developers can fix mistakes sooner and release better software with less stress.
